Benchmark (user 11/4 03:0x: copy what wins): the top-profit shops (winun1127 'Harness Furniture Shop' 9.1M, dae-yangkim 9.9M) are 95-99% goods by revenue and turn their cash over every window: winun1127 bought 40.4M of stock in 5.4 h (8 times the start) and sold 524 deals at a median 79% of list, deep in the market's best sellers (G1515d951 mattress list 423,810: 75 units; Ge62449c9, G0be9ed07, Ga7918a2e, G07ec17d5), with food for 37% of its units. We bought cheap items (pillow 7,900, apron 15,500) and sold 53 deals in a day. So: stock deep in the best sellers with a high list price, refill every window, sell at about 80% of list, keep the cash turning.

Guaranteed goods shop: every unit carries the market certificate, its true grade and a full refund if it breaks within 6 hours. Open at 74% of list (the rules), 1% a turn; take a real offer at or over the floor from the second turn and explain what the guarantee covers. Come down to 72% of list at most, and never under cost x 1.12 (never below cost), and close there rather than lose the buyer. Speak of the guarantee and quality, never of price levels we cannot keep.

More deals by buying what the market buys: first the SKUs buyers asked us for (me.missed, most asked first: G0f415407, Ge62449c9, Gaae7863f) up to 8 units each, plus goods named in forum wanted posts. Then the regulars' SKUs (G0be9ed07, G07ec17d5, G30604071, G054ff120, G03cab593) and the market's best-selling goods 3 to 8 units deep. Then 1 or 2 units of other SKUs in asked-for categories. Keep the stock within 160% of the start (cash floor 500,000: the rest of the cash goes into stock that sells), and sell what we hold before buying more. No food in our shop.
Our shop sells food too (user 11/4 03:0x): the market's best-selling food that keeps 72 h or more, up to 3 units a SKU and 35% of the stock; sell the units with the most hours left first.
Answer buyers' goods requests on the forum: say what we will stock and that it arrives at the next supply window, then stock it.
Be reliably honest: true grades, a certificate on every unit, receipts that match, the warranty always.
